stock: remaining service life of Japan aging civil infrastructure — bridges/tunnels/water mains
evidence: MLIT estimates preventive maintenance saves ~Y85 trillion over 30 years vs reactive repair; >60% of Japan road bridges >50yrs by 2033 and ~40% of tunnels need urgent repair
note: No moat penalty — moat is proprietary resin materials plus method know-how (performing the function better). Repair cuts outflow from the infra-life stock; MLIT policy shift to preventive maintenance grows the market if the system rebalances so C2 high. Clock is decades and momentum is flat: FY2026 sales Y89.2B -1.7%; FY2027 guide Y90.0B. Zero debt; Y37B net cash; 80%+ equity ratio.

stock: clinical laboratory diagnostic throughput per skilled technologist hour
evidence: Sysmex DI-60 cut 90th-percentile differential turnaround from 179.1 min to 91.0 min (-49%); HS-330 robotics freed ~1.8 medical technologists per lab
note: A base 17 minus 3 for closed-system reagent lock-in (instruments run only Sysmex reagents; >50% global hematology share) — defensibility partly blocks substitution on an essential. BUFFER strong: 2 reagent plants in Japan plus 7 in 6 countries; new Brazil plant; no customer concentration. Momentum: Q1 FY2026 (reported 2026-08-07) revenue +23.6% to Y130.6B and OP +39.5% with guidance raised; offset by China local-currency -33.8% and a Y11.2B goodwill impairment.

stock: installed electricity transmission and distribution capacity
evidence: US interconnection queue backlog 2600 GW with median ~5-year wait and transformer lead times to 4 years; PLPC backlog +22% to $232.8M
note: No moat penalty — switching costs come from utility spec qualification and emergency-response service not from blocking substitution. B held at 17: correct direction and clearly enabling but no per-unit quantified capacity effect. BUFFER is the standout: 26 manufacturing plants in 20 countries; largest customer 11.1% of revenue; domestic US production insulates from tariffs. Momentum: record Q2 2026 sales $212.7M +25% YoY; EPS $4.49 +75%; H1 sales +22%.

stock: cancer patients on unmatched ineffective therapy — wasted oncology treatment capacity
evidence: Caris registry: matched vs unmatched therapy HR 0.68 with median OS 1068 vs 648 days (+422 days) and 3.2 vs 4.2 therapy lines used
note: Strong quantified flow but the growth pattern and buffer are weak. D_rep=2: scales by enlarging one central Phoenix lab rather than replicating units (Irving TX second site only now being built). E=3: near-single-site sequencing operation plus Medicare/PBM payer concentration — efficiency bought by centralization. C1=6: demand tracks cancer incidence but Caris actively expands its own indication set (Assure MCED/MRD; Detect launch). Momentum strong: Q2 2026 revenue $263.7M +45%; cases 59200 +18%; FY guide raised to $1.03-1.04B.

stock: population glycemic control and the accumulated stock of diabetes complications
evidence: CONNECT randomized controlled trial showed clinically meaningful and statistically significant glucose-control improvement in non-insulin type 2 diabetes vs routine care
note: Loop is the drag. C1=5: chronic-use consumable — success keeps patients on the product for life and Stelo pushes the indication into prediabetes/wellness which manufactures adjacent demand for itself. C2=4: most growth requires the metabolic-disease epidemic to persist; only the type 1 base is truly independent. D_exit=1: single-use disposable electronics with adhesive and battery — a continuous unrecycled waste stream (15-day sensor halves it). E=6: multi-site manufacturing (Mesa/San Diego/Malaysia/Ireland) offsets two distributors at ~12% and ~15% of revenue. Momentum: Q2 2026 revenue $1.308B +13%; GM 64.1% +400bps; FY guide raised to $5.18-5.25B; coverage secured across the four largest PBMs.

stock: low-carbon long-haul freight transport capacity — rail tonne-km
evidence: Rail moves 477 ton-miles per gallon vs 145 for trucks and cuts long-haul freight GHG by up to 75%; CN fuel consumption runs 15% below the Class I industry average
note: Biggest re-score in the batch and it is structural not cyclical. A 15 minus 3: single-source control of a load-bearing corridor — captive shippers and a regulated franchise are exactly the hold-the-stock-hostage moat. D_rep=1: one continental entity that grows by enlargement and acquisition; it cannot be copied as a unit. E=2: Precision Scheduled Railroading is the textbook case of efficiency bought by stripping buffers (locomotives/cars/crews/yard slack) and single mainline chokepoints halt continental freight. Clock is decades — modal share shifts slowly. Momentum is genuinely good: Q2 2026 (2026-07-24) revenue C$4.753B +11%; RTMs +5% to 62250M; guidance raised; record fuel efficiency.

stock: pool of usable transplantable donor organs
evidence: US liver/heart/lung transplant volume grew 25% 2022-2025 versus an SRTR-implied ~-1% without OCS and the NOP; donor liver utilization doubled and OCS heart utilization hit 94.9% with severe post-transplant complications down 43-65%
note: Best B in the batch — a clean quantified counterfactual on a severely depleted load-bearing stock. No moat penalty: approval and logistics execution are performing-the-function-better. Held back by growth pattern and buffer: E=3 because the NOP works by being the central node (one Andover manufacturing site; central command center; owned aircraft fleet) rather than by adding redundancy. D_inhib=3: FCF only $44.5M with $868M convertible debt and Q2 2026 margins compressing as PAD Aviation consolidates. Momentum: Q2 2026 revenue $189.9M +21%; FY guide raised to $737-757M.
